quote: FSD can be derived straightforwardly: Let FZi = FTi ◦ QY ◦ FXi for i = 1, 2. If X1 ≥1 X2 and T1 ≥1 T2, then Z1 ≥1 Z2.
family: T-X{Y} decomposable family: FZ = FT ◦ QY ◦ FX

hypotheses.text: FZi = FTi ◦ QY ◦ FXi for i = 1, 2

quote: Theorem 1. Let FZi = FTi ◦ QY ◦ FXi, for i = 1, 2, where QY ◦ FX2 is convex. Let i) X1 ≥1 X2 or ii) X1 ≥2 X2 and X1, X2 belong to a location-scale family with support R. Then T1 ≥2 T2 implies Z1 ≥2 Z2.
family: T-X{Y} decomposable family: FZ = FT ◦ QY ◦ FX

hypotheses.text: FZi = FTi ◦ QY ◦ FXi, i = 1, 2, with common QY

hypotheses.formal: convexity of the composed quantile-CDF of the dominated baseline

hypotheses.text: i) X1 ≥1 X2, or ii) X1 ≥2 X2 within a location-scale family on R
hypotheses.formal: FSD in general, or SSD for location-scale

ambiguity: Order key 'icx' denotes SSD (increasing-convex order equivalent for common means); the paper uses ≥2.

quote: Theorem 2. For i = 1, 2, let FZi = FBi ◦ FXi, where Bi ~ beta(pi, qi) (qi > 1). Let FX2/(1 − FX2) be convex. Let i) X1 ≥1 X2 or ii) X1, X2 belong to a location-scale family with support R and X1 ≥2 X2. Then p1 ≥ p2 and p1/(q1 − 1) ≥ p2/(q2 − 1) imply Z1 ≥2 Z2.
family: Beta-generated (BG) family FZ = FB ◦ FX with B ~ beta(p,q); equivalent T-X decomposition B2–X{log-logistic(1,1)} with generator T = B/(1−B) ~ beta second kind and E(Ti) = pi/(qi − 1), qi > 1
compared: BG members Z1 vs Z2 differing in beta parameters and baseline CDFs

hypotheses.text: FZi = FBi ◦ FXi, Bi ~ beta(pi, qi), qi > 1

hypotheses.formal: convex odds function of dominated baseline

hypotheses.text: i) X1 ≥1 X2, or ii) location-scale on R with X1 ≥2 X2

hypotheses.formal: beta parameter ordering + B2 mean ordering (gives T1 ≥2 T2)

quantifiers: all z; qi > 1 for finite means

quote: Theorem 3. Let X and Y be RVs such that FY/(1 − FY) is convex. Let i) X ≥1 Y or ii) X, Y belong to a location-scale family with support R and X ≥2 Y. Then i ≥ j and i/n ≥ j/m imply Xi:n ≥2 Yj:m.
family: Order statistics as beta-generated distributions: Xi:n ~ beta(i, n−i+1) ∘ FX; Yj:m ~ beta(j, m−j+1) ∘ FY
compared: i-th order statistic from n iid X's vs j-th order statistic from m iid Y's

hypotheses.formal: convex odds of the dominated population

hypotheses.text: i) X ≥1 Y or ii) location-scale on R with X ≥2 Y

hypotheses.formal: printed 'i ≥ j and ni ≥ m'; proof reduces system to i ≥ j and i/n ≥ j/m (fraction rendering)

numbers: worked example: n = 35, m = 30, j = 20 gives minimum i = 24
ambiguity: The rank condition prints as 'ni ≥ m' in the text layer; from the proof and example it is i/n ≥ j/m. Both i ≥ j and i/n ≥ j/m required.

quote: Corollary 1. Let X be an RV such that the odds function FX/(1 − FX) is convex. Then: 1. Xi+1:n ≥2 Xi:n, ∀i, n (i = 1,...,n − 1). 2. Xi:n ≥2 Xi:n+1, ∀i, n.
family: Order statistics from one iid population with convex odds function
compared: adjacent order statistics within a sample; same-rank order statistics across sample sizes
ambiguity: Extends earlier Lorenz-order results of Arnold & Villaseñor (1991) and Wilfling (1996b) to SSD and a larger class.
